(a) to (d) show the distributions of contrastive accuracy 𝐴𝑐𝑐, contrastive loss L𝑐 , image reconstruction loss L𝑟𝑒𝑐 𝑖 , and visibility reconstruction loss L𝑟𝑒𝑐𝑣 when hyperparameter contrastive loss weight 𝜅 changes. (e) to further demonstrate the bivariate joint kernel density plot of each pair of losses.

Figure 2: Overview of the stage of Self-supervised Complementary Modeling (SCM). The visibility encoder E𝑣 and image encoder E𝑖 take M𝑣 and M𝑖 as input and output encoded features 𝜉 and 𝜂 in the latent space, respectively. The first pretext task helps align the encoded latent space based on contrastive learning. After performing complementary masking to 𝜉 and 𝜂 following the principles of the band limiting and image patchification, the image predictor F 𝑣→𝑖 and visibility predictor F 𝑖→𝑣 predict the masked parts of each other. Finally, visible and predicted parts are merged and decoded by visibility decoder D𝑣 and image decoder D𝑖 accordingly to complete the second pretext task of complementary masking reconstruction and output the results of M̂𝑣 and M̂𝑖 .

Figure 3: Illustration of the complementary masking in CDCRec. The sparse visibility is masked by applying band limiting, while the image is first patchified and then masked. The masked parts are depicted in black. Due to sparsity, we adopt random sampling within each band to ensure the balance between the masked and visible information.
